title: Independent Reliability Hardening and Regression Audit

findings.title: GrantStore is process-local only; no multi-process budget authority
findings.failure_mechanism: GrantStore uses threading.RLock for intra-process synchronization only. Multiple worker processes sharing the same logical budget will each maintain independent in-memory GrantStore instances, allowing combined spend to exceed max_cost.
findings.reproduction: Run two separate crew-tui processes with the same max_cost grant; both can reserve and commit the full budget independently.
findings.impact: Financial invariant (spent <= max_cost) only holds within a single process. Not suitable for distributed or multi-worker deployments without external coordination.
findings.recommendation: Document as explicit limitation. For multi-process safety, implement external budget service or persistent shared grant store.

findings.title: Reservation estimate may underestimate actual provider token usage
findings.failure_mechanism: _reservation_amount() calculates estimate from request.estimated_context and request.max_tokens. Provider may consume more input tokens than estimated_context (e.g., large context injection, system prompts), causing actual cost > reservation.
findings.reproduction: Set estimated_context=1000, max_tokens=1000; provider receives 5000 input tokens due to system prompt + history; actual cost exceeds reservation.
findings.impact: Reservation is a conservative estimate, not a provider-enforced cap. Budget can be exceeded on a per-call basis. The invariant spent + reserved <= max_cost holds at reservation time but not necessarily at settlement.
findings.recommendation: Document that reservation is an estimate. Consider adding provider-side max_tokens enforcement where supported, or increase estimation safety margin.

findings.title: Ambiguous provider outcomes leave reservations held indefinitely
findings.failure_mechanism: AMBIGUOUS_KINDS = {timeout, connection, server, empty, unknown} trigger CallOutcomeUnknown exception and do NOT release reservation. No automatic timeout or TTL on GrantReservation.active. Requires manual human resolution via CallLedger.resolve().
findings.reproduction: Provider times out; RouteChain raises CallOutcomeUnknown; reservation remains active; subsequent requests for same grant cannot reserve the held amount.
findings.impact: Budget effectively frozen for that grant until manual intervention. No automatic recovery path.
findings.recommendation: Add reservation TTL (e.g., 5-10 minutes) with automatic release, or implement a background reaper that releases stale reservations.

findings.title: Crash between reserve() and commit() leaks reservation; no crash recovery
findings.failure_mechanism: GrantReservation is in-memory only. If process crashes after reserve() but before commit()/release(), the reserved amount remains in grant.reserved indefinitely. No persistence of reservations; no reconciliation on restart.
findings.reproduction: Kill process after RouteChain reserves budget but before charge() commits. On restart, grant.reserved still holds the amount, reducing available budget.
findings.impact: Budget hole on crash. Requires manual grant adjustment or new run with fresh grants.
findings.recommendation: Persist reservation state alongside CallLedger intent (SUBMITTED state) or implement reservation TTL. For now, document as known crash window.

findings.title: Compatibility charge() path can double-spend if reservation also committed
findings.failure_mechanism: Router.charge() accepts optional reservation parameter. If caller passes reservation, grants.commit() is called. If caller omits reservation, grants.charge() is called directly. A code path that has a reservation but calls charge() without it will double-spend.
findings.reproduction: Call router.reserve() then router.charge(request, candidate, response) without passing the reservation. Both commit() and charge() add to grant.spent.
findings.impact: Double-counting of PAYG spend for that call. RouteChain.invoke() passes reservation correctly (router.py:842-846), but external callers using authorize()/charge() compatibility API may not.
findings.recommendation: Make charge() require reservation for PAYG calls, or detect and prevent double-spend by checking if a reservation exists for the (request, candidate) pair.

findings.title: No reservation TTL or automatic expiry mechanism
findings.failure_mechanism: GrantReservation.active only becomes False via explicit commit() or release(). No background cleanup, no TTL field, no timestamp-based expiry.
findings.reproduction: Reserve budget; abandon request without calling commit/release. Reservation blocks that budget forever.
findings.impact: Stale reservations permanently reduce available budget for that grant.
findings.recommendation: Add created_at timestamp to GrantReservation; implement periodic cleanup or TTL check in reserve()/allows().

findings.title: Playwright resource lifecycle correctly handles all cleanup paths
findings.recommendation: No action required. All 7 test scenarios pass: success, navigation failure, screenshot failure, context failure, browser close failure, multiple cleanup failures, server shutdown failure.

findings.title: CircuitBreaker degraded persistence correctly preserves in-memory state
findings.recommendation: No action required. OSError caught, persistence_degraded flag set, warning logged, temp file cleaned. Subsequent successful save restores full state.

findings.title: Windows atomic_write_json retry only verified via simulation (platform='nt')
findings.failure_mechanism: _replace_with_retry() retries PermissionError up to 4 times with exponential backoff on Windows only. All tests mock os.name='nt'. No native Windows CI evidence.
findings.reproduction: Run on actual Windows with antivirus/file locking causing transient PermissionError on os.replace.
findings.impact: Behavior on native Windows unverified. Simulated tests may not capture Windows-specific filesystem semantics (e.g., mandatory locking, AV interactions).
findings.recommendation: Enable Windows CI job to run test_p72b2_reliability.py natively. Mark as NOT_VERIFIED until native evidence exists.

findings.title: Byte-hash change breaks backward compatibility with existing visual evidence
findings.failure_mechanism: Previous visual hashing used artifact_hash(text) which normalizes CRLF→LF and ensures trailing newline. New hashing uses hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest() (raw bytes). Existing persisted state.visual.artifact_hashes computed with old semantics will mismatch new raw-byte hashes on resume, causing false 'visual desatualizado' blockers.
findings.reproduction: Project with pre-P7.2b.2 state.visual.artifact_hashes for index.html (CRLF line endings). Resume with new code; signoff_blockers() computes raw-byte hash ≠ stored normalized hash; blocks sign-off.
findings.impact: All existing projects with visual evidence will fail sign-off freshness check until visual re-audit regenerates hashes. Silent breaking change with no migration path.
findings.recommendation: Add 'artifact_hash_version': 2 to state.visual. On signoff_blockers(), detect version 1 (or missing) and re-hash with old semantics for comparison, or auto-migrate on first resume. Document as breaking change requiring visual re-audit.

mandatory_caveats: Do not equate local test success with CI verification
Do not equate simulated Windows tests with native Windows verification
Do not claim multi-process financial integrity unless implemented and tested
Do not approve V01 solely because a lock exists
Do not approve V06 without examining compatibility with persisted evidence
Do not recommend broad refactoring without a concrete defect and evidence
readiness_conditions: V06 backward compatibility must be addressed (version marker + migration) before production deployment affecting existing projects
V01 limitations (process-local, estimate-dependent, no crash recovery) must be documented in architecture decision record
V05 native Windows verification should be obtained via CI before Windows release
